o: Explain how language choice affects development.
c: High-level languages use readable constructs and abstractions to make software easier to develop and maintain.
Machine code consists of binary processor instructions; assembly uses mnemonics that correspond closely to processor instructions.
Assembly and machine code are tied to the instruction set of a particular processor family.
Consider readability, portability, speed requirements and direct hardware control.

m.title: Modelled explanation
m.q: A school writes a timetable application. Explain TWO benefits of using a high-level language. [4 marks]
st: Identify the command word, scenario and total marks.
Choose accurate technical terms and examples.
Connect each feature to the consequence in the scenario.

A high-level language is easier to read and maintain [1], reducing the time needed to develop or alter the system [1]. It is usually more portable [1] so the program can be adapted to different processor types with less rewriting [1].

w: A microcontroller needs precise hardware control. Explain an advantage and a disadvantage of using assembly. [4 marks]
Assembly is close to machine instructions [1], allowing detailed processor control [1]. It is processor-specific [1], so a change of hardware could require rewriting [1].
Compare high-level and low-level languages using readability and portability. [4 marks]
High-level code is more readable [1] and generally more portable [1]. Low-level code resembles processor instructions [1] and normally depends on the processor instruction set [1].
